The sample size is small, and only 22 patients completed the full 5 years of followup, RE FE RE NCE S some of whom missed scheduled evaluations.

Of those 12 patients who did not complete the full period of followup, 7 were ambulant, potentially skewing the results of the study toward those with more severe disease. Only 26 patients underwent PAIgG evaluation, limit- Ing the assessment of its association with disease duration and age of onset.

Sleep studies were performed in only 19 patients, where selec- tion bias may have contributed to more severely affected patients completing the evaluation and, thus, limiting our understanding of the spectrum of sleep disordered breathing in those earlier in their disease course. MoriYoshimura and colleagues highlight that GNE myopathy can now assuredly take its place among the expanding list of inherited myopathies associated with hematological abnormalities.19 Further prospective evaluation of the significance of PAIgG in larger patient cohorts is needed, but PAIgG appears to be a promising biomarker in this disorder.
